plan.disposition: Stage-2 scout: a single-function grammar addition (about 40 production lines, one producer fixture), classified small

findings.finding: No test covers an empty or whitespace-only quote, nor a quote made only of invisible characters (view would show an empty-looking blockquote).
findings.suggestion: Add asserts; treat a quote that is blank after stripInvisible as no quote in both mirrors.

findings.finding: Doc says a known pointer, but only the short session:ISO:n form can precede a quote; the long form followed by a quote reads as unknown (safe).
findings.suggestion: State the short form only and pin with a test assert.

findings.finding: 'never written to the log or audit' is only guaranteed for fenced entries (the form leadwright writes).
A quote containing U+2028/U+2029 fails the (.*) match, so the quote, guard and pointer are dropped silently.
Producer-shape deviations (NBSP/tab around the dash, long pointer form, unterminated quote) fall back to unknown source with no guard.
Only quotes of 20+ folded characters are guarded (QUOTE_GUARD_MIN); the doc says every folded quote is a needle.
The displayed quote is not passed through stripInvisible.

The spec/contract says the Evidence-line quote is 24–200 characters, but neither `parseEvidence` nor the guard enforces any minimum length. A short quote (e.g. `s1:...:3 — "ok"`) becomes a `foldForCompare` needle, and any edited proposed line that merely contains that common substring is then refused with 400 `line_contains_quote` — a false refusal that blocks countersign entirely (the entry stays, no way to accept it with any reasonable line). The fence-quote needles had the `> text — pointer` shape as an implicit length/structure constraint; the Evidence-line needle has none.
findings.suggestion: In `proposalFacts`, only add the Evidence-quote needle when the quote meets the contract's minimum (e.g. ≥24 chars), or skip needles below some fold-length threshold so short quotes cannot block countersign.

findings.finding: A known pointer followed by ` — ""` (empty quote) yields quote `null` but the trimmed `source` is parsed from `m[1]` while the fallback path calls `parseSourceRef(raw)` on the untrimmed original — behaviorally equivalent here, but the two paths can diverge if `parseSourceRef` ever treats whitespace differently (e.g. a padded pointer like ` s1:…:3 — "q"`: the quote path trims, the old path didn't). This is a mild inconsistency, not a concrete failure given current `parseSourceRef`.
findings.suggestion: Use `parseSourceRef(t)` in the fallback so both paths see the same trimmed input.  Test quality: the tests are substantive — they exercise real parse, guard-refusal (including case-folded repetition), audit content, and pin the fixture by hash and structure. The client unit tests would catch a wrong-quotes-order or markup regression. The e2e only covers display; guard/audit are covered server-side, which matches the AC's division. Note the second countersign test asserts the edited-line pass but does not assert the audit `data.evidence` lacks a `quote` field name — acceptable, since `not.toContain(QUOTE)` covers the text.  Regression risk: `proposalFacts`'s `pointer` variable was renamed to `source` destructuring; if `pointer` is referenced further down in the file (not shown), the diff context implies it compiles, and the exported API shapes are unchanged. `parseEvidence` is additive. No visible breakage for callers.  Spec compliance: all three AC behaviors (display-first plain text with source, copy-refusal guard, audit names source without quote) are implemented and tested. The hash pin and contract doc update match the referenced fixture.  Overall assessment: the work is sound and well-tested; the unenforced minimum quote length turning into a guard needle is the only defect worth fixing before or shortly after ship.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
